rationale: Both independently catch the strongest ground-truth theme (scope: the platform-default flip is validated only on Qwen-Image but affects every CUDA diffusion model), and both make the same sharp, unverified-in-GT catch that Part 2's switch to nn.RMSNorm makes Part 1 a no-op for Qwen-Image itself — X's enumerated model list even mirrors NumberWan's actual reply almost 1:1, giving it a recall edge. But Y's findings are more rigorously evidence-cited (explicit changed-vs-unchanged sourcing, a validated/claim-verified scan table) and it catches a subtlety X gets wrong: X asserts Cosmos3 is 'genuinely protected' by its native override, while Y shows the override only pins rms_norm/fused_add_rms_norm and silently inherits the new vllm_c-first default for every other IR op — a more precise dissection of the same scope problem. Y also ships copy-paste suggestion diffs, edging out X on actionability.
